title: Adverbs of Frequency
subtitle: Say how often something happens, and put the word in the right place.
objectives: Order adverbs of frequency from 100% to 0%
Place the adverb correctly with the verb "to be", auxiliary verbs, and other verbs
Use adverbs of frequency naturally in everyday sentences

content.intro: These small words appear in almost every conversation about routines and habits — and their position in the sentence follows a clear, simple rule.

rules.heading: Word order
rules.body:
• After the verb "to be" (am/is/are/was/were): She is always late.
  • Before other (ordinary) verbs: I always eat breakfast.
  • After the first auxiliary verb: I can never sleep on planes. / She doesn't often call.

examples: I always eat breakfast before I go to work.
She is usually tired after work.
They often watch movies on the weekends.
We never go to the beach in winter.
My brother sometimes helps me with my homework.

commonMistakes.why: With an ordinary verb (eat), the adverb goes before it, not after.
With "to be," the adverb goes after it, not before.
The adverb doesn't change the need for -s on third person singular verbs.

commonMistakes.wrong: She always go to the gym on Mondays.
commonMistakes.right: She always goes to the gym on Mondays.
commonMistakes.why: Third person singular (she) still needs -s, even with the adverb in front.

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with an appropriate adverb of frequency.

items.prompt: I ___ eat breakfast before I go to work. (100% of the time)
She ___ goes to the gym on Mondays. (80-90%)
He ___ forgets to do his homework. (10-20%)
items.explanation: "Rarely" = a small percentage of the time.

items.prompt: We ___ visit our grandparents during the holidays. (60-70%)
items.explanation: "Often" = a fairly high percentage of the time.

items.prompt: usually / I / wake up / at 7 AM
never / he / drinks / coffee / at night
always / my brother / helps / me / with chores

items.incorrect: She always go to the gym on Mondays.
answer: She always goes to the gym on Mondays.

items.incorrect: He usually wake up early in the morning.
answer: He usually wakes up early in the morning.
items.explanation: Third person singular needs -s, regardless of the adverb.

items.incorrect: We rarely goes to the park on weekdays.
answer: We rarely go to the park on weekdays.
items.explanation: "We" doesn't take -s in the present simple.

summary: Scale: always (100%) → usually → often → sometimes → rarely → never (0%).
The adverb goes after "to be," but before an ordinary verb.
With an auxiliary verb (can, do, will), the adverb goes right after the first auxiliary.
